feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(3,2)$ and passes through the point $(21,-4).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(3,2)$ into the above gives

$$
{(y-2)}^{2}=4p(x-3).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(21,-4),$ we substitute $x=21$ and $y=-4$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(-4-2)}^{2} & =4p(21-3) \\ {(-6)}^{2} & =4p\cdot (18) \\ 36 & =72p \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =2(x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-2)^{2} & =2(x-3) \\ 4 & =2(x-3) \\ 2 & =x-3 \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $5.$
